item.title: Power Grid Future
item.description: The Texas power grid survived last week’s freeze but, with a rise in data centers, there are worries that — next time — we won’t be so lucky. Experts are downplaying the concerns. Professor Joshua Rhodes at UT Austin says the developers are building their own generators. But, he says the operators of the power grid will still have handle demand from a growth in population. The latest census numbers show that around one-thousand people are moving to Texas each day.

item.title: Bible Books Errors
item.description: A Bible-infused elementary school curriculum, which was approved by the state of Texas two years ago, is riddled with errors. Pam Little, who sits on the State Board of Education, says there were 42-hundred mistakes in the so-called Bluebonnet materials. Most, she says, were formatting errors, typos and incorrect page numbers. She lashed out at the publisher, calling them “sloppy.”

item.title: AG Commish Race
item.description: Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller is suddenly facing headwinds in his run for re-election. First it was Governor Greg Abbott who endorsed his opponent, Nate Sheets. Now, Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham has done the same. She accused Miller of “misconduct and misbehavior.” Last year, one of Miller’s former friends told a Texas Ranger that the commissioner asked him to dispose of three bags of marijuana and gummies because he was afraid that the DEA might find them on his property.

item.title: Justice Department Says It’s Taken Down Epstein-Related Files That May Have Had Victim Information
item.description: By MICHAEL R. SISAK and LARRY NEUMEISTER Associated Press NEW YORK (AP) — The Justice Department said Monday that it had taken down several thousand documents and “media” that may have inadvertently included victim-identifying information since it began releasing the latest batch of documents related to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein on Friday. It blamed the release of sensitive information that drew an outcry from victims and their lawyers on mistakes that were “technical or human error.”
